summary.text:
Cheltenham's 2025/26 outturn is a seven-page appendix to Council on 20 July 2026. Total CFR £229.377m at 31 March 2026 (GF £119.942m + HRA £109.435m). External borrowing £217.435m at 3.86% weighted, split PWLB £134.030m at 3.38%, a single bank fixed-term £8.900m at 3.82%, and £74.500m of LA short-term at 5.10%. The last LOBO — £5m Bayerische Landesbank at 3.95% — was called in May 2025 at a proposed 7% and the council refused, repaid, and replaced through the LA short-term market. Internal borrowing £11.950m; the balance-sheet identity ties within £8k. £7m pooled fund book (CCLA Property, CCLA Diversified, Schroders Income Maximiser) with a cumulative unrealised capital loss of £824k on original investment; in-year dividends 4.36% (£305k) and capital gain £15k. Treasury outturn came in £172k adverse to revised budget, driven by the HRA capex under-delivery reducing the HRA share of the debt recharge (£165k of the £172k).

The loan book reconciles on 52 of our 53 rows. One row of ours — 883445, £18m at 4.05% maturing December 2026 — is inconsistent with the council's own reported PWLB movement (their book fell £3.430m in the year, which cannot accommodate an £18m live loan on top). Excluded, the remaining 52 loans total £134,034,920 at a coupon-weighted 3.379% against the council's printed £134.030m at 3.38%. Principal ties to £5k, weighted rate ties to two decimal places. Same bc-loans data-lag class flagged in EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md; investigation task raised. The 53rd row is disclosed in the email rather than glossed.

Two hooks worth writing. The Bayerische call is a specific, dated data point in the LOBO-refused sequence the pipeline has been tracking (≥11 calls logged, Bayerische new to that count). The refused 7% was reached by the LA short-term market itself in February and March 2026 — the sequel to the decision is testable in the same paper. And the front-end concentration (38% under 12m, £82.500m, mostly the £74.500m LA short at 5.10%) sits in a market whose recent peak was 7% and whose direction after the US/Iran war escalation (§3.7) was for the market to price in rate hikes. Neither is advice; both are calibrations. The paper also flags £38.500m of grandfathered commercial-purpose PWLB (§3.10) which is left out of the email because 'commercial' framing carries policy overtones. Email drafted; blocks only on address — the appendix carries no officer contact block, and the covering committee report is not in our hand. State: drafted-needs-address per PIPELINE.md.

officer.subject: May's Bayerische LOBO call at 3.95% to 7% — and the sequel in your own Table 3
officer.body:
Hi,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on Appendix 7 that went to Council on 20 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Yours is a short and cleanly written outturn; this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A loan-book cross-check first, and I'll declare our own gap up front. Our file of your PWLB carries fifty-three rows; one of them — an eighteen-million maturity loan at 4.05% dated to run to December 2026 — doesn't fit the movement your own Table 3 shows (£137.459m to £134.030m, a fall of £3.430m in the year cannot accommodate an eighteen-million live loan on top). We're treating it as a stale row on our side and investigating; if you're happy to tell us we've caught it right we'd be grateful, but this isn't an invitation to correct our file. Drop that one row and the remaining fifty-two loans total £134,034,920 at a coupon-weighted 3.38% against your Table 3's £134.030m at 3.38%. Principal ties to five thousand pounds, the rate ties to two decimal places. And the balance-sheet identity closes to eight thousand pounds without needing to strip anything out — CFR £229.377m less external £217.435m leaves £11.942m of internal borrowing, against the £11.950m you print in Table 1.

The reason we wrote is section 3.6. The Bayerische Landesbank LOBO you'd been carrying at 3.95% was called in May last year at a proposed 7%, and you refused, repaid, and replaced it with LA short-term. That's one datapoint of many in a sequence we've been tracking across the sector — at least eleven LOBO calls we've logged since the pipeline started, refused every time; Bayerische Landesbank hadn't yet appeared in that count. The interesting bit is your own section 3.8: the LA market you moved into then rose to peak at around 7% in February and March 2026. Put another way, the alternative to that call arrived at the same headline rate about fourteen months later. The £74.5m of LA short-term the year-end table shows at 5.10% was struck earlier and cheaper — but any of it that rolls in the summer prices against a fresh curve, and section 3.7 notes markets were pricing in hikes after the US/Iran war escalation. Not a recommendation; a calibration. The place to watch where the LA market is clearing week to week is pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, which publishes every loan the sector draws each month.

The wider shape of the position. Thirty-eight per cent of the whole book sits under twelve months (£82.5m, still comfortably below your 50% ceiling), and most of that is LA short. At the other end, twenty-nine per cent (£62.720m per your Table 8) is beyond ten years — essentially all PWLB, and paying at that weighted 3.38%. Your own liability benchmark isn't shown in the appendix, but the interactive version of that indicator — which CIPFA is putting closer to centre stage in the code updates — is at pwlbtoday.org/liability-benchmark and rebuilds live off the curve for any council whose CFR and reserves are printed.

Your own book, priced daily against the DMO's premature-repayment curve, is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. Break costs are indicative only — only the DMO can quote a binding number, and we model no MRP or accounting treatment.

On training, three fit Cheltenham. LOBO management and negotiation, on the back of the Bayerische decision — you've already lived the mechanics but the course covers the reply arithmetic for the next one. Strategic PWLB borrowing, for whenever the LA market becomes uncomfortable enough to term out. And Short-term borrowing and cashflow management, because that's where £74.5m of your book currently sits. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 (Appendix 7), Council, 20 July 2026 — https://democracy.cheltenham.gov.uk/documents/s54684/appendix-7-treasury-management-outturn-report-2025-26.pdf

officer.reconciliation: PRINCIPAL: £134,034,920 (ours, 52 of 53 loans) = £134.030m (theirs, Table 3) — ties to £5k. WEIGHTED RATE: 3.379% (ours) = 3.38% (theirs) — ties to two decimal places. IDENTITY: CFR £229.377m − external £217.435m − OLTL £0 (not printed) = £11.942m = Internal (over) borrowing £11.950m (Table 1) — ties within £8k rounding. OUTLIER DISCLOSED: our 53rd row (883445, £18m 4.05% mat 2026-12-03) is inconsistent with the council's own reported PWLB movement; declared in the email as a stale row on our side, not framed as an invitation to correct us.
